I want to develop a m-itx case and I've already got a rough prototype built in solidworks. I have addressed problems I've found in my own build but I want to get some feedback from y'all about what you don't like about cases you've used. When I get this finished I plan on opening it up for other people to have access to.

TLDR; What do you like/not like about the m-itx cases you've seen?

they dont have enough air flow and they restrict potential overclock. Youre gpu is much more likely to thermal throttle. you can fix these issues with water cooling but youll spend much more to get the same performance that you could of got with a full tower and air coolers.
I've really been working on the airflow. I haven't made a physical prototype but I've started doing some flow analysis and air cooling should work fine.

i had my 3570k and gtx780 in a haf 932 and my temps were great. Then i put my 3570k and 780 in a bitfenix prodigy and my gpu was constantly hitting 80c and thermal throttling and downclocking. I even tried putting them in a nzxt s340 and i was having the same issue. Now I use the nzxt s340 with no case fans but with the side panel off and a gtx 970 and my 3570k at 4.5ghz on a cheap air cooler. Getting the 970 made the biggest difference. my pc was pulling 400w from the wall 780 and im down to like 250w with the 970. That 780 was dissipating a lot of heat in side my case. I personally would rather have my pc to be quiet than small. im considering getting a full tower again and selling this nzxt s340 to someone that wants something cute.
Those are some pretty high temps. Are you pretty much maxing out your hardware when you put it under load?
80c is just when nvidia 700 and 900 series cards start throttling. yes i would say im maxing out my hardware. i have a 144hz monitor so my card is generally trying to achieve 144fps.

If I ever were to design a small case myself I have always wanted to try something similar to what Apple did with the Mac Pro chassis. Position mounts and fans in a way that allows you to have a single, central column of air in a line. So all the hot air gets pushed into the column and subsequently pushed through the case. In my head it seems like a cool idea but I haven't done the testing required to determine its viability with thermal tests or anything. Feel free to play around with the concept, I'd be interested to see what you can come up with

Being able to disassemble them easily and quickly would be a huge benefit. Particularly when you are pushing the limits of what a small case can handle by putting in really high end hardware you might need to reorganize the layout of the case to accommodate that 980ti or equivalently long card. I would be hugely impressed if you made the inter-workings of the case modular and easily movable bays and mounts to offer a large variety of build options.

Side note, I would love to offer any additional help in terms of critiques or ideas so please feel free to message me if you would like my two cents!

http://i.imgur.com/QnGkVRl.jpg

http://i.imgur.com/2tRXW1N.jpg

The second pic is a crude mockup of how things would be in the case. Not alot of options but in there respective spots you would have a wide variety. Any size card would fit or you could slap a liquid cooler in there if you are using it as a HTPC

The first thing that I would ask you is if you could move the WAN Show-esque mesh logo over the CPU to give it open access to exhaust. That way the CPU isn't contributing to internal temps as severely.

My second comment is in regards to the GPU, it seems a bit strangled in its current orientation. You would be golden if you could have it exhaust out of the case instead of into the close quarters. You're going to need a PCI extender regardless so you might as well have the GPU face up. so keeping it where it is but facing up and then adding some sort of removable crossbar to prevent sag. You would also need to add some more of the meshing obviously so it can breathe

With this tight of a case you really want to avoid the collection of hot air in the case because it will heat up at an exponential rate as the ambient temp rises causing a lot of throttling. The best way in my experience to deal with this is to just have all the heat generating components have access to fresh air.

Aside from those two heat/airflow comments I think you have a really solid case here and I am interested in seeing this project as it progresses.

The top vent is actually positioned directly above the cpu and I love the idea to flip the gpu. The bottom of the case has the same sort of vent for the psu. The only problem I run into is that not every card is going to have the same position of the fan. I need to come up with some sort of design that will accommodate all possible positions

You might be stuck going with a more ubiquitous opening similar to the one on the Silverstone SG13 which is essentially just a big rectangle over that whole area above the GPU. While this might detract from the aesthetic to a degree I think the temperature benefits are wholly worth it,
